results.title: Verbose database errors returned to client
results.root_cause: The 500 on malformed input is caused by the unparameterized, %-formatted SQL in search_claims (the same SQL injection as the companion finding); the verbose-error part (CWE-209) does not reproduce on main because FastAPI's default handler returns a generic 500.
results.evidence: search.py:7-8 "... WHERE member_id = '%s' AND description LIKE '%%%s%%' ..." % (member_id, term); run locally: GET /claims/search?q=x' -> 500 with body 'Internal Server Error' (no DB text); q=%' OR 1=1 -- -> 200 with all 5 claims across members. main.py has no debug=True or custom exception_handler.

results.title: ACM certificate expires in 12 days
results.root_cause: Operational cert-expiry notice for an imported ACM certificate; the repo has no aws_acm_certificate resource and no reference to status.example.com, so there is no defect in this repo.
results.evidence: grep for 'acm' / 'status.example' across the repo (excluding tickets.json) returns nothing; infra/ contains only s3.tf, iam.tf, compute.tf, providers.tf, variables.tf.

results.title: Insecure direct object reference - any claim readable by any member
results.root_cause: get_claim loads the claim by id alone and never compares row.member_id to the authenticated user or checks role, so any member can read any claim (IDOR).
results.evidence: routes.py:17 db().execute("SELECT * FROM claims WHERE id = ?", (claim_id,)) and returns dict(row) without an ownership check; run locally: token-alice (m-100) GET /claims/1003 -> 200 with member_id m-200 record. IDs are sequential integers (1001-1005 in db.py).

results.title: Static cloud credentials shipped with the portal application
results.root_cause: A static AWS access key pair is committed in the portal's config file, which config.js loads and ships with the app, instead of using an instance role or secrets manager.
results.evidence: default.json:6 "accessKeyId": "AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE", :7 "secretAccessKey": "wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY"; src/config.js:5-6 reads config/default.json directly; .gitignore does not exclude config/.

results.title: SAST: Route handler with no authorization check (CWE-639)
results.root_cause: Same defect as PEN-2024-021: the /claims/{claim_id} handler resolves the path identifier without comparing it to the authenticated principal; it is the only path-parameter route in services/claims-api/app.
results.evidence: routes.py:15-20 @router.get("/{claim_id}") def get_claim(claim_id: int, user=Depends(current_user)): row = db().execute("SELECT * FROM claims WHERE id = ?", (claim_id,)) and user is never used. /claims/search is scoped by user_id, so it is not this finding.

results.title: Shell spawned by application process (doc-svc-prod-01)
results.root_cause: A shell spawned by the doc_service.app process matches exploitation of parse_manifest's unsafe yaml.load(raw, Loader=yaml.Loader), which lets an uploaded manifest build arbitrary Python objects (for example !!python/object/apply:os.system), giving command execution.
results.evidence: upload.py:15 manifest = yaml.load(raw, Loader=yaml.Loader); app.py:11-15 passes the raw POST /upload body to parse_manifest; alert parent 'python3 -m doc_service.app' -> child '/bin/sh -c id' on doc-svc-prod-01 (compute.tf aws_instance.doc_service Name tag).

results.title: Role credentials used for unusual API calls
results.root_cause: The doc-service-prod instance role carries an inline policy of Action "*" on Resource "*", so instance-metadata credentials (probably taken through the doc-service RCE) can call iam:ListRoles, s3:ListAllMyBuckets and secretsmanager:ListSecrets, far beyond its s3 Put/Get baseline.
results.evidence: iam.tf:19-26 Statement = [{ Effect = "Allow", Action = "*", Resource = "*" }] on role aws_iam_role.doc_service (name doc-service-${var.env}, env default prod), attached to aws_instance.doc_service via aws_iam_instance_profile.doc_service (compute.tf:4).

results.title: portal deploy to the new region failed, wrong credentials?
results.root_cause: Operational DR bug: the portal's AWS region is hardcoded to us-east-1 in a single static config file with no env/region override, so a us-west-2 deploy keeps the old region and keys. This is a config-portability defect, not a new vulnerability, though it sits next to the hardcoded keys from PEN-2024-029.
results.evidence: default.json:5 "region": "us-east-1" right next to the static keys at :6-7; config.js only reads config/default.json (no process.env); infra/variables.tf region default "us-east-1" and s3.tf has a single demo-health-member-docs bucket with no DR replica.

results.title: Remote code execution via config/manifest upload
results.root_cause: parse_manifest deserializes the uploaded YAML manifest with the unsafe full yaml.Loader instead of yaml.safe_load, so python object constructor tags run arbitrary code on the upload host.
results.evidence: upload.py:15 manifest = yaml.load(raw, Loader=yaml.Loader); app.py:13-15 raw = environ['wsgi.input'].read(size); manifest = parse_manifest(raw), no auth on POST /upload. Impact grows because the host role has Action "*" (iam.tf aws_iam_role_policy.doc_service).

results.title: upload hangs on large YAML manifests
results.root_cause: Performance/operational issue, not a security defect: legitimate ~4MB manifests fit under MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES (5MB) and are parsed synchronously in the request by PyYAML's slow pure-Python yaml.Loader on a single-threaded wsgiref server, so the request appears to hang.
results.evidence: upload.py:4 MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024 (4MB passes); upload.py:15 yaml.load(raw, Loader=yaml.Loader) (pure Python, not CLoader); app.py:28 wsgiref make_server(...).serve_forever() is single-threaded. Same line as the CWE-502 bug, but this ticket describes benign large input, not exploitation.

results.title: Rate limit threshold exceeded - public marketing site
results.root_cause: Operational noise: WAF rate-limit rule correctly blocked a crawler on the marketing site, and nothing in this repo defines CloudFront or WAF (the closest thing is the public-by-design static_site_assets bucket).
results.evidence: Alert says action=BLOCK, note 'crawler, robots respected after block'. grep for cloudfront/waf across infra/ and services/ finds nothing. infra/s3.tf:31 marks static_site_assets as 'Public by design', DataClass=public.

results.title: SAST: Possible SQL injection (CWE-89) - 1 finding, HIGH
results.root_cause: search_claims builds its SQL with Python % string formatting, so the user-controlled search term q goes unparameterized into db().execute().
results.evidence: search.py:7-8 "FROM claims WHERE member_id = '%s' AND description LIKE '%%%s%%' " ... % (member_id, term); line 10 db().execute(query). term comes from GET /claims/search?q= (routes.py:11-12) and only has a max_length=200 limit.

results.title: Privilege escalation path: instance profile to admin
results.root_cause: The inline policy doc-service-access on role doc-service-prod grants Action "*" on Resource "*", which includes iam:* and sts:*. The role reaches EC2 doc-svc-prod-01 through aws_iam_instance_profile.doc_service.
results.evidence: iam.tf:23-24 Action = "*", Resource = "*" in aws_iam_role_policy.doc_service (role = aws_iam_role.doc_service.id, name doc-service-${var.env}=prod). aws_instance.doc_service (compute.tf:4) has iam_instance_profile = aws_iam_instance_profile.doc_service.name and tags Name=doc-svc-prod-01, Service=doc-service.

results.title: member saw someone else's claim
results.root_cause: GET /claims/{claim_id} looks up the claim by id alone and never checks that it belongs to the authenticated member, so any authenticated user who loads a claim-detail URL with another member's id gets that member's claim (IDOR).
results.evidence: routes.py:17 db().execute("SELECT * FROM claims WHERE id = ?", (claim_id,)) has no member_id filter, and `user` from Depends(current_user) goes unused. Contrast search, which scopes by user['user_id']. The member-portal has no claim-detail route, so the claims-api endpoint is what serves it. The exact bookmark mechanism is not proven.

results.title: DLP: PII pattern in outbound attachment (resolved)
results.root_cause: Corporate DLP event on an employee laptop: the email was blocked, the file was reviewed and found to be a synthetic test fixture, and the ticket is closed. No code or config defect in this repo.
results.evidence: Alert JSON: action=blocked, review='test fixture file with synthetic values, closed', asset 'corp laptop LT-4412'. No service or infra in the repo is involved.

results.title: IAM user with long-lived access key (key age 412 days)
results.root_cause: The portal-svc IAM user's long-lived static access key is hard-coded in the member-portal's committed config, so the key can't be rotated without a code change and stays exposed in git history. The service should use role-based temporary credentials instead.
results.evidence: default.json:6 "accessKeyId": "AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE", line 7 "secretAccessKey": "wJalr...EXAMPLEKEY". Other tickets in tickets.json tie key 'AKIA...MPLE' to principal portal-svc. infra/ has no aws_iam_user, so the user itself is not managed in this repo.

results.title: S3.8 - S3 Block Public Access setting should be enabled at bucket level
results.root_cause: The PHI bucket demo-health-member-docs has all four S3 Block Public Access flags set to false, which lets the public bucket policy (aws_s3_bucket_policy.member_docs) take effect.
results.evidence: s3.tf:11-14 block_public_acls=false, block_public_policy=false, ignore_public_acls=false, restrict_public_buckets=false. aws_s3_bucket.member_docs (s3.tf:1-7) has bucket=demo-health-member-docs and tags DataClass=phi, Service=doc-service.

results.title: doc-service can write to buckets it shouldn't
results.root_cause: The doc-service role's inline policy allows Action "*" on Resource "*", which implicitly grants s3:PutObject on every bucket, including the analytics bucket.
results.evidence: iam.tf:23-24 Action="*", Resource="*". The policy is attached to role doc-service-prod and reaches the doc-service host via aws_iam_instance_profile.doc_service. In code, doc_service/storage.py only targets DOCS_BUCKET (demo-health-member-docs), so write access to the analytics bucket comes from IAM, not the app. No analytics bucket is defined in infra/.

results.title: IAM.1 - Policies should not allow full '*' administrative privileges
results.root_cause: The inline policy doc-service-access on role doc-service-prod grants full admin (Action "*" on Resource "*"), and the role is reachable from the doc-service instance profile.
results.evidence: iam.tf:17 name = "doc-service-access"; role = aws_iam_role.doc_service.id (name doc-service-${var.env}, env default prod); lines 23-24 Action="*", Resource="*". aws_iam_instance_profile.doc_service (iam.tf:29-32) is used by aws_instance.doc_service.

results.title: Member documents retrievable without authentication
results.root_cause: The bucket policy on demo-health-member-docs grants s3:GetObject on every object to Principal "*", so anonymous users can read member documents. The predictable members/<ref>/<type>/<file> keys let an attacker enumerate other members' documents.
results.evidence: s3.tf:22-26 Sid="AllowDocLinks", Effect=Allow, Principal="*", Action="s3:GetObject", Resource="${aws_s3_bucket.member_docs.arn}/*". The policy is enforceable because the public access block is disabled (s3.tf:11-14). Key layout comes from doc_service/storage.py:7 f"members/{member_ref}/{document_type}/{filename}".

results.title: Secret detected: AWS access key id (CWE-798)
results.root_cause: An AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded in the committed member-portal config file default.json (loaded by src/config.js loadConfig()), and they are in git history (commit f9af89b).
results.evidence: "accessKeyId": "AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE", "secretAccessKey": "wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY". Note: these exact values are AWS's published documentation example pair, so they are probably not a live credential, and src/ only reads config.aws.region. Committing credential fields to the repo is still the defect.

results.title: S3.2 - Bucket policy grants read to Principal '*'
results.root_cause: False positive: demo-health-static-site-assets is meant to be public. It is tagged DataClass=public / Purpose=public-website and holds only marketing assets, so anonymous GetObject is the intended behavior and no sensitive data is exposed.
results.evidence: infra/s3.tf:31 comment '# Marketing site assets. Public by design: logos, CSS, help-center images.'; aws_s3_bucket.static_site_assets tags DataClass="public", Purpose="public-website"; policy Sid "PublicWebsiteRead" allows only s3:GetObject; block_public_acls/ignore_public_acls=true. Compare aws_s3_bucket_policy.member_docs (PHI), which is the real exposure.

results.title: SAST: Unsafe YAML deserialization (CWE-502)
results.root_cause: parse_manifest() deserializes the raw POST /upload body with yaml.load(..., Loader=yaml.Loader), the full/unsafe loader. A request-supplied manifest can therefore build arbitrary Python objects, which can lead to code execution.
results.evidence: upload.py:15 `manifest = yaml.load(raw, Loader=yaml.Loader)`; app.py:13-15 `raw = environ["wsgi.input"].read(size)` -> `parse_manifest(raw)` with no auth.

results.title: document links keep working after logout
results.root_cause: The PHI bucket demo-health-member-docs has a bucket policy that grants s3:GetObject to Principal "*", and its public access block is fully disabled. EOB document URLs therefore work anonymously with no session or authorization.
results.evidence: aws_s3_bucket_policy.member_docs: Sid "AllowDocLinks", Effect Allow, Principal "*", Action "s3:GetObject", Resource "${aws_s3_bucket.member_docs.arn}/*"; aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block.member_docs all four flags = false; bucket tag DataClass="phi"; doc-service storage.py writes members/{member_ref}/... keys to this bucket.

results.title: EDR: generic trojan detection on build agent (false positive)
results.root_cause: Operational noise, not a repo defect: an EDR heuristic false positive on a packed esbuild binary in the npm cache of build agent build-agent-07. The analyst has already confirmed it as a known FP and allowlisted the hash.
results.evidence: verdict "Generic.Trojan.Heur" on /tmp/npm-cache/.../esbuild; analyst_note "known FP on packed node binaries, vendor case opened, hash allowlisted". The repo has no build-agent config, and member-portal does not declare esbuild as a direct dependency.

results.title: Sequential resource enumeration detected
results.root_cause: GET /claims/{claim_id} loads a claim by its sequential integer id and never checks that the claim's member_id matches the authenticated user (IDOR). A single member token can therefore enumerate and read every member's claims.
results.evidence: routes.py:17 `db().execute("SELECT * FROM claims WHERE id = ?", (claim_id,))` returns dict(row) with no `user["user_id"]`/role check; `user` from Depends(current_user) is unused. IDs are small integers 1001-1005 (db.py SEED_CLAIMS). Matches principal token-***bob (m-200) with 598 distinct 200s.

results.title: WAF signature match: SQLI_PATTERN_UNION_SELECT (x37)
results.root_cause: search_claims() builds its SQL by %-formatting the user-controlled q term into the query string, which is then executed. The UNION SELECT payloads from the WAF alert (rule in COUNT mode, so forwarded to origin) reach an injectable query.
results.evidence: search.py:7-8 `"... WHERE member_id = '%s' AND description LIKE '%%%s%%' ..." % (member_id, term)` then `db().execute(query)`; routes.py:10-12 /claims/search passes q (max_length=200 only) straight in.

results.title: Authenticated SQL injection in claims search endpoint
results.root_cause: search_claims() string-formats the search term into a SQL query against the sqlite claims table. The payload ' OR '1'='1 escapes the LIKE literal, drops the member_id filter and returns other members' claims, and sqlite_master can be extracted.
results.evidence: search.py:7-8 `"FROM claims WHERE member_id = '%s' AND description LIKE '%%%s%%'" % (member_id, term)`; search.py:10 `db().execute(query)` with no bound parameters; db.py uses sqlite3 (hence sqlite_master).

results.title: secure message inbox times out for long-tenure members
results.root_cause: Not a security issue: the inbox timeout is a performance problem caused by a missing (member_id, created_at) index on the messages table. The inbox query is fully parameterized, so it is not SQL injection.
results.evidence: services/member-portal/src/messages.js:1-2 comment 'The table has no index on (member_id, created_at), so large inboxes scan the full table.'; messages.js:3-8 INBOX_SQL uses `?` placeholders and `db.query(INBOX_SQL, [memberId, `%${term}%`])` binds values.

results.title: Claim identifiers are predictable
results.root_cause: Same defect as SIEM-88275: get_claim() has no ownership/authorization check on the claim it loads. Predictable integer IDs make bulk retrieval easy, but they are a contributing factor, not the root cause.
results.evidence: routes.py:16-20 `def get_claim(claim_id: int, user: dict = Depends(current_user))` -> `SELECT * FROM claims WHERE id = ?` and returns the row without comparing row['member_id'] to user['user_id']; db.py:16-17 `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` with sequential seeds 1001-1005.

results.title: Excessive instance role permissions amplify host compromise
results.location: infra/iam.tf:16-27 aws_iam_role_policy.doc_service (attached via aws_iam_instance_profile.doc_service -> aws_instance.doc_service in infra/compute.tf:4)
results.root_cause: The doc-service EC2 instance role's inline policy grants Action "*" on Resource "*" (full admin), so anyone executing code on doc-svc-prod-01 inherits admin-level AWS access.
results.evidence: iam.tf:21-25 Statement = [{ Effect = "Allow", Action = "*", Resource = "*" }] on role aws_iam_role.doc_service; compute.tf:4 iam_instance_profile = aws_iam_instance_profile.doc_service.name with tag Name = "doc-svc-prod-01". Contrast claims_api policy scoped to secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on claims-api/*.

results.title: MFA reset request - contractor laptop replaced
results.root_cause: Routine IT/helpdesk MFA reset request for a replaced contractor laptop; no identity-provider code or config exists in this repo and no defect is implied.
results.evidence: Repo contains only claims-api, doc-service, member-portal and infra (S3/IAM/EC2) Terraform; no IdP/MFA configuration anywhere. claims-api/app/auth.py uses static demo tokens and notes 'Real deployments use the identity gateway.'

results.title: S3.2 - Bucket policy grants read to Principal '*'
results.root_cause: The bucket policy on the PHI bucket demo-health-member-docs grants s3:GetObject to Principal "*" and the public access block is fully disabled, making all member documents world-readable.
results.evidence: s3.tf:22-26 Sid="AllowDocLinks", Principal = "*", Action = "s3:GetObject", Resource = "${aws_s3_bucket.member_docs.arn}/*"; s3.tf:11-14 block_public_policy=false, restrict_public_buckets=false; bucket tags DataClass = "phi" (s3.tf:5). Not the static_site_assets bucket, which is public by design (DataClass=public).

results.title: PyYAML 5.3.1 - CVE-2020-14343 (CRITICAL, 9.8)
results.root_cause: parse_manifest deserializes untrusted upload manifests with yaml.load(..., Loader=yaml.Loader) (the unsafe full-object loader), so the vulnerable PyYAML 5.3.1 is reachable and arbitrary code execution is possible; upgrading to 5.4 alone would not fix it since yaml.Loader remains unsafe.
results.evidence: upload.py:15 `manifest = yaml.load(raw, Loader=yaml.Loader)` where raw is the POST /upload body (app.py:11-15); requirements.txt:1 `PyYAML==5.3.1`.

results.title: suspicious email reported by employee
results.root_cause: Phishing email report on corporate mail (look-alike domain, no credentials entered) is corporate IT/mailbox noise unrelated to any code or infrastructure in this repo.
results.evidence: No email/mail-handling code or config in repo; domain benefits-demohealth.example.com is not referenced anywhere; ticket already routed to mailbox team for blocking.

results.title: search box breaks when you type an apostrophe
results.root_cause: search_claims builds the SQL query with Python %-string formatting of the user-supplied search term, so an apostrophe terminates the string literal (syntax error 500) and the endpoint is SQL-injectable.
results.evidence: search.py:5-8 "FROM claims WHERE member_id = '%s' AND description LIKE '%%%s%%' " % (member_id, term); search.py:10 db().execute(query) with no bind params; reached via GET /claims/search?q= (routes.py:10-12). The portal's own inbox search (member-portal/src/messages.js:3-8) is parameterized, so this is the claims-api defect.

results.title: Anomalous query volume - claims-api-prod-01
results.root_cause: A single caller getting ~350x normal rows per query on claims-api-prod-01 is consistent with exploitation of the unparameterized LIKE term in search_claims (e.g. q=' OR '1'='1) bypassing the member_id filter and dumping all claims.
results.evidence: search.py:7 `WHERE member_id = '%s' AND description LIKE '%%%s%%'` % (member_id, term) — injected term can append OR conditions/UNION to return every row; no LIMIT on the query. Host maps to aws_instance.claims_api (compute.tf:11-17, Name=claims-api-prod-01). The /claims/{claim_id} IDOR (routes.py:15-20) returns only one row per request so would not raise rows_returned_p99.

results.title: Unauthenticated object reads on sensitive bucket
results.root_cause: Anonymous GETs across 1,102 keys of demo-health-member-docs are possible because the bucket policy grants s3:GetObject to Principal "*" with public access block disabled on this PHI bucket.
results.evidence: s3.tf:24-26 Principal = "*", Action = "s3:GetObject", Resource = "${aws_s3_bucket.member_docs.arn}/*"; s3.tf:12,14 block_public_policy=false, restrict_public_buckets=false; tags DataClass="phi"; doc-service stores member docs at members/{member_ref}/... in this bucket (storage.py:3-7).

results.title: Unexpected outbound connection from doc-svc-prod-01
results.root_cause: A first-seen python3 egress from doc-svc-prod-01 is consistent with code execution via the unsafe yaml.load(Loader=yaml.Loader) on attacker-supplied upload manifests (the upload RCE referenced in PEN-2024-034).
results.evidence: upload.py:15 `yaml.load(raw, Loader=yaml.Loader)` on POST /upload body (app.py:11-15) allows !!python/object/apply payloads (e.g. os.system/urllib) executed by the python3 service process; host is aws_instance.doc_service (compute.tf:1-9, Name=doc-svc-prod-01).

results.title: API call from access key outside normal network
results.root_cause: The portal-svc AWS access key and secret are hardcoded in the committed member-portal config file, so the leaked long-lived key is being used from outside the VPC.
results.evidence: default.json:6 "accessKeyId": "AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE" (matches alert key AKIA...MPLE), default.json:7 "secretAccessKey": "wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY", default.json:8 docsBucket demo-health-member-docs (alert api s3:ListBucket).
